title: The inside of my mind
intro: Drag to look around. Walk with WASD or the arrow keys. On a phone, use the pad in the corner.

landmarks.name: The tree of life
landmarks.body:
Pomul vieții, the tree of life, is one of the oldest motifs in Romanian embroidery. It has a trunk, symmetric branches and a star at the top.

This one is generated by code, cell by cell. The lines on the ground that start at its roots connect it to every other place here.

landmarks.name: The code garden
landmarks.body:
These screens show code from my projects. There is the potential field from ZEPHYR, the CPPN from DAEDALUS, the p5.js sketch that draws the tree behind you, and the shader that gives this landscape its look.

I enjoy writing code as much as drawing, and I like code that other people can read easily.

landmarks.name: The listening ring
landmarks.body:
Sixteen pillars, each tuned to one note of a scale used in Romanian doina music. The music gets louder as you walk closer, and the pillars move with it. Walk between two pillars to play their notes.

Music is important to me, and I think about rhythm and melody in a similar way to loops and patterns in code.

landmarks.name: The colour field
landmarks.body:
A torus knot that changes colour, shapes inside other shapes, a harmonograph that draws itself, and a painting generated by a small network.

I paint, draw digitally and sketch. Colour and shape are often where my ideas start, before I write any code.

landmarks.name: The flight field
landmarks.body:
A small drone flies between obstacles. The lines on the ground show the potential field it follows.

This is ZEPHYR, my thesis project, shown as a visual piece instead of a plot in a paper.

landmarks.name: The loom
landmarks.body:
A loom that weaves on its own. Each new row is computed from the row before it by a simple rule, like a cellular automaton. Above it turns ochiul boului, the eight pointed star from Romanian embroidery.

Traditional patterns and code both repeat a small rule to build something larger.
